did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a precise date: in the eighth month, in the second year of King Darius. It records the word of the Lord that came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo the prophet.
The Lord reminds the new generation of His anger toward their ancestors, so they can learn from the past and not repeat their ways.
The central message of the chapter is the call: “Return to Me … and I will return to you”—turning back to the Lord also brings the promise of His presence.
Zechariah raises a question that encourages reflection on previous generations: the ancestors and the prophets do not live forever, but the word of the Lord continues to stand.
The prophets’ words did indeed come true: the ancestors acknowledged that the punishment that came upon them was in accordance with their ways and deeds.
The first vision is also given a precise date: on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shevat, in the second year of Darius.
In the night vision, Zechariah sees a man riding a red horse among myrtle trees, with red, sorrel, and white horses behind him.
The horses and riders in the vision are described as messengers whom the Lord sent to patrol the earth and observe its condition.
The messengers report that the whole earth is at rest and peaceful. Yet against this backdrop of calm, a prayer is heard for Jerusalem and the suffering cities of Judah.
The angel of the Lord asks how long the anger against Jerusalem and the cities of Judah will continue, noting that seventy years have passed since the destruction and punishment.
The Lord’s answer to the angel includes “good and comforting words” and expresses His great zeal for Jerusalem and Zion.
The Lord announces that He is very angry with the nations that are complacent, because they abused the limited punishment imposed on Israel and made matters worse.
The Lord promises to return to Jerusalem with mercy. As part of this promise, His house will be rebuilt there, and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
The chapter ends with hope: the cities of Judah will overflow with prosperity, the Lord will comfort Zion, and He will once again choose Jerusalem.
